correctness.rationale: Independently reconstructed full reachability for a binary dot-product model of the Fano plane, reversing moves from distributions already occupying each target, in increasing weight. Every reverse step removes one at an occupied recipient and adds two at a neighbor; each such parent has a legal forward move. An explicit point-line relabeling to the cyclic model gives exact agreement with all 38,760 frozen mask rows, 161 optima, and 42 slide and jump edges (21 three-vertex paths and 98 isolated vertices). Counting every permutation of the seven points preserving the lines and composing with the dot-product duality gives all 336 automorphisms, because the connected bipartition is unique and a side-preserving permutation is determined by its point permutation. The four geometric class orbits have sizes 21,42,56,42. The repaired proof uses the known profile restriction, but determines geometry without counting solutions: target weight strictly excludes misplaced same-side two piles and noncollinear triples, and at weight exactly one the two opposite singleton lines must each receive a delivery from the heavy point and then can only send to distinct points on the target line. Nonincident 3+3 piles cannot interact after either first move. Explicit routes establish each case of sufficiency, including splitting two deliveries through the intersection of the two-pebble line and a remote target line in the 4+2 case. Basis changes and duality give transitivity in each geometrically distinguished family. This reconstructs necessity, sufficiency and the orbit partition in the repair.
residual_risks: The repair uses an exact finite classification of admissible pile-size profiles as input; its geometric refinement is analytical. Fixed Heawood graph and ordinary target-by-target pebbling only, not simultaneous covering or pegging.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The slack-threshold theorem covers the frozen minimum-size transfer results outright, not the geometric orbit partition. Bounds on optimum size and results for other move systems do not classify labeled ordinary placements; the scalar optimum is not reasserted as new.

evidence: The broad finite decision procedure can of course decide individual instances. Its published counts do not force, for example, the exclusion of noncollinear and mixed-side 4+1+1 placements. Within that profile the repair uses both subunit target weights and a separate obstruction at weight exactly one, plus constructive routes on marked Fano triples.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: This is not merely evaluating the earlier recurrence on a new sample or computing automorphisms of a listed table. It supplies a geometry-based membership condition and a proof within the known pile profiles, using explicit reachability and exclusion arguments beyond orbit transitivity alone.

evidence: 99c7c303db16 uses precisely the same ordinary pebbling and solvability conventions, but states only the three pile profiles for weight six. 9b97498f2d8d is on the same Levi graph and gives Fano incidence types for pegging, where the initial configuration is a vertex subset and the legal move consumes pegs from distinct neighbors along a path.
The same-date Heawood Lipschitz-free-ball result has facets as its objects, and the matched-apex pebbling result has a universal-vertex hypothesis.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Considered point-line duality and the flag/nonflag formulation rather than comparing titles. A dual statement of the geometric condition would be equivalent, but neither the pile profiles alone nor orbit results for the different pegging game identify these four classes.

originality.rationale: The frozen package's scalar optimum, total census, three pile-size profiles, and both optimal relocation graphs have exact coverage in the broader Heawood slack-threshold record. They are now credited as background rather than claimed. The surviving distinct finding identifies the four full orbits by a necessary-and-sufficient Fano incidence rule, and proves the incidence mechanism. The compared source's weight profiles do not specify which supports with those profiles work; its transfer edge and component counts do not supply that rule. This is a scope assessment, not a finding of chronological priority.
residual_risks: Dates of distinct catalogue records do not establish derivation or priority.
The Muntz et al. full text was not recovered; a scalar implication or unlocated structural description remains possible. No empty search was treated as evidence of absence.

value.rationale: The repair turns an optimum size and unordered pile-profile census into a local, geometry-based test for exactly which configurations work. This makes all optimum states describable by four representatives with explicit transitivity and provides a route or an obstruction for each configuration type, including the sharp target-potential equality case. It is a natural finite classification useful for studying solvable configurations on this incidence graph, not just retabulating the covered minimum or transfer counts.
residual_risks: The contribution is an exact structural description on one graph; no application to other games or graph families is inferred.
